question: According to Appendix F of SP 800-37 Rev. 2, what distinguishes an initial authorization, an ongoing authorization and a reauthorization (including how a reauthorization review can differ from the initial one), and what items does an authorization package include?

facets.text: Initial authorization: the initial (start-up) risk determination and risk acceptance decision based on a complete, zero-based review of the system or common controls.

evidence.quote: Initial authorization is defined as the initial (start-up) risk determination and risk acceptance decision based on a complete, zero-based review

facets.text: Ongoing authorization: subsequent risk determinations and acceptance decisions at agreed-upon, documented frequencies; time-driven or event-driven; dependent on a robust continuous monitoring program.

evidence.quote: Ongoing authorization is defined as the subsequent (follow-on) risk determinations and risk acceptance decisions taken at agreed-upon and documented frequencies
is dependent on a robust continuous monitoring program

facets.text: Reauthorization: a static, single point-in-time decision after initial authorization (under ongoing authorization usually event-driven); the authorizing official may choose a complete zero-based review or a targeted review based on the triggering event.

evidence.quote: Reauthorization is defined as the static, single point-in-time risk determination and risk acceptance decision that occurs after initial authorization
the authorizing official can choose to initiate a complete zero-based review of the system or of the common controls or to initiate a targeted review

facets.text: Package item: executive summary.

evidence.quote: Executive summary

facets.text: Package item: security and privacy plans.

evidence.quote: Security and privacy plans

facets.text: Package item: security and privacy assessment reports.

evidence.quote: Security and privacy assessment reports

facets.text: Package item: plans of action and milestones.

evidence.quote: Plans of action and milestones

reference_answer: Initial authorization is the start-up risk determination and acceptance based on a complete, zero-based review. Ongoing authorization is the follow-on series of risk determinations and acceptances at agreed, documented frequencies (time- or event-driven), relying on robust continuous monitoring. Reauthorization is a static, point-in-time decision after the initial one - under ongoing authorization usually event-driven - and unlike the initial authorization the authorizing official may choose either a full zero-based review or a targeted review tied to the triggering event. The authorization package contains an executive summary, security and privacy plans, security and privacy assessment reports, and plans of action and milestones.
notes: Appendix F (PDF pp.158-160, printed 139-141). The package list straddles the page break (two items on each page). Footnote 128 lets the AO require extra artifacts (e.g. risk assessments) - not part of the base list. The Glossary splits the same content into six items (security and privacy plans/reports listed separately); equivalent. Appendix F's later reauthorization discussion (pp.171-172) restates the same distinction and is acceptable evidence for f3.

evidence.quote: NASA report guidelines did not call for lists of figures/illustrations or lists of tables favored by prescriptive sources

reference_answer: Five deviations: (1) the symbols list is body matter after the introduction rather than front or back matter; (2) tables and figures may be (and often are) grouped in back matter after the appendixes and references instead of appearing in the text soon after first mention; (3) since 1977 the COSATI standard title page with the abstract is the last page, rather than the abstract being front matter; (4) the manual calls for both an abstract and a summary, which most textbooks and style manuals do not recommend; (5) no lists of figures/illustrations or of tables are called for.
notes: CONCLUSIONS - Sequential Components, PDF p.107 (printed 95). The preceding paragraph lists components NASA omitted (memo/letter of transmittal, list of illustrations, recommendations, glossary) - related but not the 'deviations' list.

question: According to the GPT-3 paper's appendix on total training compute, how many petaflop/s-days were used to train GPT-3 175B and T5-11B, why is T5's flops per parameter per token half of GPT-3's, and how many flops is one petaflop/s-day?

facets.text: GPT-3 175B: 3.64E+03 petaflop/s-days (3.14E+23 flops).
T5-11B: 3.82E+02 petaflop/s-days (3.30E+22 flops).
T5 is an encoder-decoder model, so only half of its parameters are active for each token (3 vs 6 flops per parameter per token).

evidence.quote: since T5 uses an encoder-decoder model, only half of the parameters are active for each token during a forward or backwards pass

facets.text: One petaflop/s-day = 8.64e+19 flops.

evidence.quote: We report both flops and petaflop/s-day (each of which are 8.64e+19 flops)

reference_answer: Table D.1: GPT-3 175B used about 3.64E+03 PF-days (3.14E+23 flops); T5-11B about 3.82E+02 PF-days (3.30E+22 flops). T5's flops per parameter per token are 3 instead of 6 because, as an encoder-decoder, only half of its parameters are active for each token. One petaflop/s-day equals 8.64e+19 flops.
notes: Appendix D, PDF p.46 (Table D.1, Docling #/tables/19). Main text (p.39) only says 'several thousand petaflop/s-days' for 175B; Figure 2.2 is a plot. For T5 the 'fwd-pass flops per active param' value of 1 already folds in the 0.5 active fraction (2 x 0.5), so 1 x 3 (backward-pass multiplier) = 3 flops per parameter per token, versus 2 x 3 = 6 for GPT-3; the 'frac of params active' column is informational.
